newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela meets Zaire's Kabila.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela meets Zaire's Kabila.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila arrived at President Nelson Mandela's private home in Johannesburg on Wednesday for closed-door talks on South African attempts to assist in negotiations for peace in eastern Zaire.
Kabila arrived at Mandela's Houghton suburb home at 1615 GMT in a white mini-bus escorted by members of the South African Intelligence Service.
A government official told reporters at the house that there would be no photo opportunities of the meeting and no media statement would be released on the content of the talks.

The talks follow an announcement by African foreign affairs ministers on Wednesday in Tripoli to hold an urgent summit on the situation in Central Africa on March 18-19. A location for the summit of heads of state still has to be decided.
Mandela agreed to meet Kabila after his return from Botswana on Wednesday, where he attended a Commonwealth policy meeting on governance in Africa.

Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters Mandela remained committed to an early meeting with Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, and would probably travel to Zaire with other African leaders for the talks.
"His idea is that a delegation of heads of state should go to Zaire to meet President Mobutu there," Mankahlana said.
Mandela told reporters earlier this week he hoped to meet Mobutu in Kenya or Zaire on March 19. Officials said this date had however not been confirmed.

Mankahlana said Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad, who on Wednesday anchored proximity talks involving Kabila, briefed Mandela at the Waterkloof military airbase near Pretoria before he travelled to Johannesburg to meet the rebel leader.
Earlier this week South African government officials said Mandela would probably not meet Kabila, who arrived in South Africa on Tuesday.
Diplomats said U.S. Assistant Secretary of State George Moose, who is visiting South Africa, also met Kabila on Wednesday.

Officials declined to say whether Pahad was able to report progress to Mandela, who last week announced a new South African-led initiative for peace in Zaire, where the government is fighting ethnic Tutsi rebels.

Mankahlana said Mandela, who leaves for Southeast Asia on Friday, wanted to give his personal encouragement to the peace process, about which officials and diplomats have so far remained tight-lipped.
"The President expressed the wish to meet Kabila and shake his hand. The President is not going to go into any hard discussion.
"The intention is to encourage Kabila to play the role that President Mandela believes he is capable of playing in Zaire. Kabila is obviously a very important player," he said.
Kabila's rebels, many of them Zairean Tutsis whose ethnic kin control neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi, took up arms last October and have overrun a swath of east Zaire's borderlands.

The conflict, which escalated this month with the aerial bombing of rebel-held towns, has sent tens of thousands of refugees fleeing and threatens to destabilise Zaire and its Central African neighbours.
